evidence: Quadrupole mass spectrometry (QMS) measurements were performed in situ using an RGA200 (Stanford Research Systems) whereby residual precursor and reaction byproduct gases were differentially pumped through a 35 μm orifice that samples reaction chamber exhaust. In situ QCM measurements were performed with a modified reactor lid wherein mass changes may be monitored in situ directly adjacent to and simultaneous to ex situ film growth as previously described. Ex situ spectroscopic ellipsometry (Woollam M2000 V VASE) was utilized to evaluate film thicknesses using optical constants from literature. X-ray diffraction (XRD) measurements were acquired with a Bruker Advance D8 Powder X-ray Diffractometer. Surface Raman spectroscopy measurements of films were taken with a Innovative Photonics Solutions 100 mW 785 nm laser. Thickness and composition were collaborated by scanning electron microscopy (SEM) on a Phenom ProX equipped with an energy dispersive X-ray spectroscopy (EDX) detector for elemental analysis. Atomic force microscopy (AFM) was used to observe surface features.
